reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The current reward achieves 80% success_like_terminal_rate with stable touchdowns, but the dense positive budget (1512.78) is much larger than the objective positive budget (62.2), giving a dense_to_objective_ratio of 0.25. The policy can accumulate large rewards by staying near the pad with low velocity and upright angle, without needing to terminate. This explains the 20% timeout rate where the policy hovers on the pad collecting dense rewards. The reward_payment_audit flags main_engine_firings and orientation_engine_firings as raw_action_bonus_terms, but these are diagnostic-only variables not part of the reward sum. The real issue is the dense_to_objective_ratio: the objective bonus is relatively too small compared to the dense progress rewards, so the policy prefers to delay termination to collect more dense rewards. The previous successful edit (iter_004->iter_005) added a time_bonus (one-shot terminal bonus for early termination) which improved fitness_score by +11.06. However, the dense_to_objective_ratio remains high (0.25), and the policy still times out 20% of the time. The failed patterns show that reducing dense rewards (iter_002->iter_003) or increasing success_bonus alone (iter_003->iter_004) both caused regression to hovering. The successful pattern was adding a time_bonus, which increased the objective budget without reducing dense rewards. The current edit should further increase the objective budget by adding a larger time_bonus for very early termination (e.g., 100 for episode length < 300) to make quick termination even more attractive, while preserving the existing dense rewards and success_bonus.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: The dominant components by absolute return are orientation_engine_firings (302.0), distance_to_pad (269.93), main_engine_firings (240.8), both_legs_contact (214.8), vertical_speed_reward (160.21), distance_reward (151.01), success_bonus (60.0). The first four are diagnostic-only and not part of the reward sum. The actual reward components are balanced with no single component dominating (dominance_ratio 1.12 for orientation_engine_firings, but that's diagnostic). The dense positive budget (1512.78) is much larger than the objective positive budget (62.2), meaning the policy can accumulate large rewards by staying near the pad with low velocity and upright angle, without needing to terminate. This may explain why the policy sometimes times out (20% timeout rate) while collecting dense rewards on the pad. The time_bonus (mean 30.0) adds to the objective budget but is still small relative to dense rewards.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions are used (coverage_ratio 1.0). The dominant action is 2 (main engine) at 36.5%, followed by 1 (left orientation) at 31.1%, 0 (do nothing) at 17.7%, and 3 (right orientation) at 14.6%. Since all actions are already used, the issue is not action coverage but trajectory-phase guidance: the policy learns to reach the pad and then stay there to collect dense rewards, rather than terminating quickly.
reflection_diagnosis.failed_pattern_reuse_check: Three failed patterns are explicitly forbidden: (1) Reducing distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, and angle_reward scales (iter_002->iter_003 caused -23.96 fitness drop and regression to hovering). (2) Increasing success_bonus from 100 to 200 alone (iter_003->iter_004 caused -290.79 fitness drop and regression to hovering). (3) Increasing repeatable per-step bonuses without event/progress gating. The successful pattern (iter_004->iter_005) that improved fitness by +11.06 was adding a time_bonus (one-shot terminal bonus for early termination). The current edit will follow this successful pattern by adding a larger time_bonus for very early termination (episode length < 300) to further increase the objective budget and reduce the dense_to_objective_ratio. This avoids all three forbidden patterns.

This follows the successful pattern from iter_004->iter_005 (adding time_bonus) which improved fitness_score by +11.06. The bonus is event-gated (paid only at termination) and one-shot (paid once per episode). This makes termination relatively more attractive compared to collecting dense rewards, encouraging the policy to land quickly and terminate. The bonus is scaled to be comparable to the success_bonus (100) to provide a meaningful incentive without dominating.
